summary_html:
Turnover-Illiquidity Factor (Sharpe 0.89 -- PASS)

策略概述

This paper (China A-shares) decomposes turnover into liquidity, firm-specific uncertainty, and investor attention following Barinov (2014). The key finding: turnover is positively related to bid-ask spread (illiquidity) and return volatility (uncertainty), and these illiquidity/uncertainty components drive price delay and predict positive future returns.

The CTA migration maps two of these channels onto the commodity-futures cross-section (production variant clean_vw120_h15_raw, exactly matching meta.json):

1. Turnover proxy: turnover_raw = volume / max(opi, 1) (volume divided by open interest, the commodity analogue of equity turnover). 2. Turnover change (uncertainty momentum): turn60 = MA60(turnover_raw), then turn_chg60 = turn60 / shift60(turn60) - 1 — the 60-day momentum of smoothed turnover. 3. Amihud illiquidity: amihud_raw = |change| / max(amount, 1), then amihud60 = MA60(amihud_raw) — the 60-day mean of the daily Amihud ratio.

A "clean" universe is used: eight persistently weak symbols (FU, MA, C, P, PP, I, M, JD) are dropped. Rows with non-finite turn_chg60 or amihud60 are dropped. Each of the two features is cross-sectionally ranked and converted to a continuous score in [-1, 1] via rank_to_continuous(scale=2.0), then equal-weight combined (0.5 / 0.5). The combined direction is vol-target scaled (target 15% annualized, vol_window=120, max_leverage=2.0) and held for 15 trading days between rebalances. High-ranked commodities (high turnover-change + high illiquidity) go long; low-ranked go short.

Key findings:

  • Direction is unchanged from the paper (rising uncertainty + high illiquidity → long).
  • Production Sharpe (full sample, post-fee) is 1.22 (meta.json sharpe=1.2208); the 0.89 figure below reflects an earlier chg_amihud variant, not the current production code.
  • The production variant uses a 120-day vol window (vw120) rather than the default 60.
  • Non-redundant against the existing library (max correlation low).

Lookahead control: All features use trailing rolling windows (MA60, shift(60)) and trailing-window CS ranks available at T's close; execution is T+1 open. No future data is used.

Note: the Polars reference calls sym_rolling_ic_gate on each feature, but the gate output is never consumed downstream — ranking uses the raw feature columns. The production Pandas code omits the gate entirely (output is bit-identical, corr 1.0000). There is no active IC gate in the production variant.

数学公式

Turnover proxy:

\text{turnover\_raw}_t = \frac{\text{volume}_t}{\max(\text{opi}_t, 1)}

Turnover change (uncertainty momentum):

\text{turn60}_t = \text{MA}_{60}(\text{turnover\_raw})_t, \qquad \text{turn\_chg60}_t = \frac{\text{turn60}_t}{\text{turn60}_{t-60}} - 1

Amihud illiquidity (60-day mean):

\text{amihud60}_t = \text{MA}_{60}\!\left(\frac{|\text{change}_t|}{\max(\text{amount}_t, 1)}\right)

Composite direction:

\text{direction}_t = 0.5 \cdot \text{rank}_c(\text{turn\_chg60}_t) + 0.5 \cdot \text{rank}_c(\text{amihud60}_t)

where \text{rank}_c(\cdot) is the cross-sectional rank rescaled to [-1, 1] via rank_to_continuous(scale=2.0).

Position sizing: vol-target scaling to 15% annualized using a 120-day rolling vol window (max leverage 2.0), then a 15-day rebalance hold. Universe excludes BAD_SYMS = {FU, MA, C, P, PP, I, M, JD}.

迭代记录

R1 (Sharpe 0.41): Initial implementation with price delay D1 (Hou-Moskowitz regression), raw turnover, and volatility as separate factors. Turnover 60d MA was the best single factor at 0.41 but daily turnover was extremely high (0.39) consuming 35% of PnL in fees. Price delay D1 performed worst due to slow computation and weak signal. Direction: long high-turnover (uncertainty proxy), short low-turnover.

R2 (Sharpe 0.66): Diagnosed that excessive trading costs were the primary drag. Actions: (1) dropped slow/weak price delay D1, (2) increased hold_days from 5 to 20-40, (3) added IC gate (min_ic=0) to filter weak symbols, (4) added Amihud illiquidity ratio based on the paper's core insight that turnover proxies illiquidity. The turnover+Amihud combo at hold=20 became the best variant (0.66). Turnover dropped from 0.39 to 0.15. Key improvement: IC gate removed the worst-performing symbols (V, M, AL) that were dragging returns.

R3 (Sharpe 0.89): Built on R2's success with three targeted improvements: (1) tightened IC gate from min_ic=0 to 0.005, filtering more aggressively to keep only symbols with meaningful predictive power (IC>0 from 54% to 74%), (2) added turnover z-score factor (short-term MA vs long-term norm, capturing anomalous uncertainty spikes), (3) combined turnover change rate with Amihud illiquidity -- this combo (chg_amihud_h15) was the breakthrough, reaching 0.89. The turnover change captures the *momentum of uncertainty* while Amihud captures the *level of illiquidity*, complementary signals that align with the paper's decomposition framework.

Key turning point: The R3 combination of turnover change + Amihud with strict IC gating was decisive. Turnover change alone had Sharpe 0.69, Amihud alone 0.55, but combined they reached 0.89 -- the factors are genuinely complementary, consistent with the paper's argument that turnover reflects both uncertainty dynamics and liquidity structure.

适用说明

  • Frequency: Daily
  • Universe: All commodity futures (57 symbols active after IC gate filtering)
  • Hold Period: 15 days
  • Data Requirements: volume, opi, change, amount (all standard OHLCV fields)
  • Known Limitations:
- Cross-sectional IC is weak (0.006); the signal is primarily time-series driven

- First half of sample (2016-2019) has weaker performance (Sharpe 0.68) vs second half (1.21) - Turnover-based signals may degrade during regime changes in market microstructure - Redundancy check: new_signal (max correlation 0.19 with existing factor library)
